validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed. CAC-4 is one of four genuinely distinct historical parallel lines in the Central Asia–Center (Средняя Азия–центр) system that GEM already carries as SEPARATE rows — CAC-2 (P2291), CAC-3 (P2292), CAC-4 (this row, P5770), CAC-5 (P5771) — matching the real-world CAC-1/2/4/5 eastern branch + CAC-3 western branch structure (confirmed via en.wikipedia + karakalpak blog). This is NOT a duplicate: the four rows describe four physically different pipes built in different years, not one pipe counted twice. Direct 2023-dated proof of ongoing physical operation: Intergas Central Asia's own 2023 Annual Report (АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия» за 2023 год, verified live, one of the sheet's own gem.wiki citations) names «САЦ-4» and «САЦ-5» explicitly as active assets that underwent major capital repair in 2023 (823 km across 14 sections, cost 24,840 million tenge) to enable a new Russia→Uzbekistan reverse-flow transit inaugurated 7 Oct 2023 (6.5 bcm/y rising to 10 bcm/y). A 2019 Нефть и газ academic-journal article (also one of the sheet's own citations, verified live) independently confirms the system continues to transit gas through Kazakhstan under Intergas Central Asia's operation. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are trivially correct — every source calls this a «магистральный газопровод» (trunk/transmission gas pipeline).

validity.recommendation: Update: re-derive CAC-4's own individual Capacity and Length — do not treat 60.2 bcm/y (or the ~3,700–3,962 km corridor length) as this single line's own figures without a per-line source. Also verify StartYear1: 3 independent non-GEM pages unanimously give 1973, not GEM's 1976.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=60.20 bcm/y is IDENTICAL across three separate GEM rows for three different historical CAC lines: P2291/CAC-2 (len 2,662 km), P5770/CAC-4 (len 3,700 km, this row), P5771/CAC-5 (length blank) — while a fourth, P2292/CAC-3, carries a different value (5.0). The only figure I could independently verify for '60.2 bcm/y' comes from a 2019 Нефть и газ journal article (http://neft-gas.kz/f/zhd_osmanov_pv_klimov.pdf, confirmed live and read via pdftotext -layout — the url_verifier substring screen misses it on this PDF, a known Cyrillic-PDF false negative per its own docstring), which states it for the 'Средняя Азия–центр' TRANSIT SYSTEM AS A WHOLE (Uzbekistan→Kazakhstan→Russia direction): 'с пропускной способностью – 60,2 млрд м3/год, протяженностью – 3 962 км', not of any one parallel line. That system-total length (3,962 km) is close to but does not match P5770's own claimed 3,700 km, and other independent sources put the whole-corridor length even higher (~4,892 km per a secondary web summary). I found no source giving CAC-4's OWN individual capacity or length distinct from the corridor total — energybase.ru (which gem.wiki cites for this figure) is IP-blocked from my location, and a 2013 university-library PDF citation for it (library.tou.edu.kz/fulltext/bibl/b794.pdf) is now dead (HTTP 404, confirmed via url_verifier). This is the same 'one system capacity stamped on multiple strings' pattern flagged elsewhere in this sweep (P2291/P5770/P5771 vs. P2292) — recommend Update research each string's true individual throughput rather than accepting the identical 60.2 on three rows. Separately: StartYear1=1976 conflicts with three independently-authored, non-GEM pages that unanimously give 1973 for CAC-4's commissioning — Karakalpakstan Blog 2017 ('CAC-4 was commissioned in 1973'), English Wikipedia 'Central Asia–Center gas pipeline system' (same wording), and Russian Wikipedia 'Газопровод центральная Азия — центр' ('4 — в 1973 году'). These three are not fully independent of each other in ultimate primary sourcing, but all three disagree with GEM's 1976 in the same direction and I could not corroborate 1976 anywhere. Diameter (1015/1220/1420 mm) is plausible — falls within the sourced system-wide range (1,020–1,420 mm) and Intergas's 2023 report separately names a 'Loop MG CAC-4' (Лупинг МГ «САЦ-4») which would plausibly carry a different diameter than the main line — but no source attributes these three exact figures to CAC-4 specifically, so it stays unresolved rather than confirmed.

validity.recommendation: Update: correct Owner1 — evidence points to Intergas Central Asia (wholly-owned subsidiary of QazaqGaz / Samruk-Kazyna, i.e. the Kazakh state), not Gazprom PJSC 100%, as the owner/operator of this pipeline's Kazakh segment.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Owner1 = 'Gazprom PJSC' at 100%. Two independent sources contradict a 100%-Gazprom ownership claim. (1) Intergas Central Asia's own official 'General Information' page (intergas.kz/ru/obwaya-informaciya/, verified live) states the company is part of «АО «Национальная компания «QazaqGaz»» (Kazakhstan's national gas company) and that it operates the trunk pipelines, explicitly including «МГ «Средняя Азия - центр» с луйпингами» (the CAC trunk pipeline system with loopings) across multiple regional management units — no mention of Gazprom ownership anywhere on the page. (2) A 2011 Samruk-Kazyna press release (sk.kz/press-center/news/56766, verified live) describes a 'dispatcher agreement between the dispatch centers of Central Asian gas transporters — JSC Intergas Central Asia [and] Gazprom' and a mid-term Gazprom–Intergas transportation CONTRACT (2011–2015) for gas transiting Kazakh territory — i.e. Gazprom appears as a transportation CUSTOMER/counterpart under a services contract, not as owner of the Kazakh pipeline asset. Given this row is scoped to the Kazakhstan gas tracker and its Kazakh segment is what Intergas Central Asia (state-owned) physically operates and repairs (see the 2023 Annual Report cited under the existence finding), a blanket 'Gazprom PJSC 100%' owner attribution looks wrong or at minimum badly oversimplified for an internationally-routed pipeline (Turkmenistan→Uzbekistan→Kazakhstan→Russia) whose Kazakh portion is demonstrably run by a Kazakh state company. I did not find any source stating Gazprom owns 100% of this asset; recommend Update research whether GEM's convention wants Owner split by country segment or reassigned to Intergas Central Asia / QazaqGaz.

summary: P5770 (CAC-4) exists and is correctly classified — confirmed via Intergas Central Asia's 2023 Annual Report and a 2019 industry journal (not a duplicate of GEM's separate CAC-2/CAC-3/CAC-5 rows). Two concerns staged: SPEC (Capacity=60.2 bcm/y is identically duplicated across 3 GEM rows and matches an independent source's WHOLE-SYSTEM total, not CAC-4's own throughput; Length=3,700km likewise close to a whole-corridor figure not a per-line one; StartYear1=1976 conflicts with 3 sources giving 1973) and ATTRIBUTION (Owner1='Gazprom PJSC 100%' contradicted by Intergas Central Asia's own site + a Samruk-Kazyna release, which point to Kazakh state ownership/operation). 6 refs added (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location, plus two blank Location sub-fields deep-filled); Start/Capacity/Length/Diameter/Owner left UNRESOLVED pending Update.
